name: Critical Mineral Recycling: Li-ion Black Mass & E-Waste Urban Mining
scope: India's Rs 1,500 cr Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme, battery EPR rules and the listed companies moving from scrap handling and black mass into lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper and precious-metal recovery.

summary.one_line: The scheme is now in its execution phase: 58 recyclers are cleared and pledged capacity is about 3x the target, but no subsidy has been paid yet. Listed exposure is still thin. Gravita's Q2 FY27 results (27 Oct) were driven by copper with no Li-ion disclosure, and the stock is down about 19% over a year. Eco Recycling's eligibility remains provisional, so the theme is clearly not priced in.
key_points: PIB confirms the Ministry of Mines found 58 entities eligible: 20 on 30 Mar 2026 and 38 on 29 Apr 2026. They pledged about 850 KTPA of capacity and about Rs 5,000 cr of investment. Financial support will be considered only after capacity development and start of production (S1, S2).

Pledged capacity is about 3.1x the Cabinet target of at least 270 kt/yr, but pledged investment is below the ~Rs 8,000 cr expected. The scheme pays a 20% capex subsidy plus a back-ended opex subsidy, capped at Rs 50 cr per large entity and Rs 25 cr per small one (S4).

Gravita's Q2 FY27 (Sep quarter, reported 27 Oct 2026): consolidated net profit was about Rs 102 cr, up from about Rs 96-97 cr, and below a Rs 107 cr estimate. Consolidated revenue was reported at Rs 1,427-1,445 cr (+36-38% YoY) because RMIL copper was added, while standalone revenue fell to Rs 786.91 cr from Rs 852.20 cr (S8, S9, S10). No Li-ion figures were disclosed.

Gravita's Li-ion business is still R&D-stage. On the Q1 FY27 call, management said it is 'doing R&D to set up our own processing unit for black mass' and that 'the quantity of black mass is also less' (S7). Its 6,000 MTPA Mundra plant, which cost about Rs 14 cr (S6), is about 1.2% of the 4.97 lakh MTPA group capacity (S7).

Eco Recycling holds a provisional JNARDDC eligibility letter dated 30 Apr 2026, disclosed to BSE (S5). Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 76% YoY to Rs 16.20 cr, but PAT grew only 3% to Rs 6.90 cr (S16).
Refining is still the bottleneck and is mostly in private hands (Attero, Rubamin, Exigo). Shredders say overseas payables beat domestic ones, and black mass exports need MoEF&CC/DGFT approval (S17).

The theme is not priced in. Gravita closed at Rs 1,323.30 on 28 Oct 2026, down 19.3% over one year and 28.8% year to date (S10). On 31 Oct, screener.in put Gravita 27.5% and Eco Recycling 32.4% below their 52-week highs (S25).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Small e-waste recyclers, for which an incentive of up to Rs 25-50 cr (S4) is large against revenue. Eco Recycling's FY26 standalone revenue was Rs 48.18 cr (S5).
Recyclers with collection networks and EPR clients, as battery EPR recovery targets rise to 90% for EV and portable batteries from 2026-27 (S21).
Integrated metals players with smelters to absorb feed, such as Hindalco's PCB e-waste plant at Pakhajan, which recovers mainly copper plus rare earths and special metals (S18).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Pure shredders (R2) if black mass export checks tighten. Black mass is hazardous waste under HS 8549 and needs MoEF&CC and DGFT approval to export (S17).
Domestic refiners face a feedstock squeeze. Most end-of-life feed today is LCO cells from consumer electronics, not EV packs (S17). Gravita's management also calls black mass availability low (S7).
Investors relying on headline scheme numbers: 850 KTPA is pledged capacity, not built capacity, and money flows only after production starts (S1).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Gravita's Q2 FY27 concall transcript, for any update on Li-ion black mass processing or a scheme application (S7, S8).
Eco Recycling's Q2 FY27 results (no date found) and any decision on its proposed Rs 100 cr critical-minerals recovery project (S15).
The first capacity-commencement notices and subsidy releases under the scheme (S1).
An official list naming the 58 entities. None has been published in PIB or press coverage (S1, S2).

sections.title: What critical mineral recycling means in India

subsections.title: Black mass, hydromet refining and urban mining

blocks.text: Li-ion recycling has two steps. First, spent cells and gigafactory scrap are discharged, shredded and separated into 'black mass', whose price depends largely on cobalt content. Second, hydrometallurgical (hydromet) refining turns black mass into lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese salts. Indian recyclers that only shred are called R2 recyclers; one industry participant estimates they make up over 80% of the industry (S17). E-waste 'urban mining' recovers copper, precious metals and some rare earths, mainly from printed circuit boards. Hindalco's Pakhajan plant is one example (S18).

items: Eligible feedstock under the scheme: e-waste, Li-ion battery scrap, and other scrap such as catalytic converters from end-of-life vehicles. Both new units and expansions of existing ones qualify (S4).
Officials say incentives are linked to actual mineral recovery rather than black mass production alone, and the scheme covers 27 critical minerals (S3).
Gravita's management argues that value stops at black mass for a plain shredder: 'we do not want to get into a normal product… We want to go into value-added products' (S7).

subsections.title: Where the value chain is thin

blocks.text: Most of India's black-mass refining sits with unlisted companies. EVreporter lists Attero at up to 15,000 MT/yr of black mass, Rubamin at 10,000 MTA, Exigo at 7,600 MTA and ADV Metal Combine licensed for 2,500 MT/yr. It also quotes Rubamin as saying government-backed refining capacity is 'already short of feedstock' (S17). No listed company has disclosed a commissioned hydromet refinery. Eco Recycling reports pre-processing with hydromet as its preferred route (S14). Namo eWaste is still seeking a technology tie-up (S22). Gravita is doing R&D on a black mass processing unit (S7).
The listed theme today is front-end collection and shredding. The refining step, which the scheme is designed to reward, is largely in private hands (S3, S17).

sections.title: Scheme, EPR rules and pledged capex

subsections.title: How the Rs 1,500 cr scheme works

blocks.caption: Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Critical Mineral Recycling: key terms
rows: 3 Sep 2025, under the National Critical Mineral Mission
Notified 2 Oct 2025; applications 2 Oct 2025 to 1 Apr 2026; JNARDDC is the Project Management Agency
20% on plant, machinery, equipment and associated utilities, for starting production within a set timeframe
40% in year 2 and 60% in year 5 on reaching incremental-sales thresholds
Rs 50 cr per large entity (opex cap Rs 10 cr); Rs 25 cr per small entity (opex cap Rs 5 cr)
One-third of outlay for small and new recyclers, including start-ups
At least 270 kt/yr recycling capacity, ~40 kt/yr critical mineral output, ~Rs 8,000 cr investment, ~70,000 jobs

blocks.title: Scheme capacity: Cabinet target vs pledged by 58 approved entities

blocks.text: PIB confirms 58 eligible entities across battery recycling, e-waste processing and other waste recovery: 20 cleared on 30 Mar 2026 and 38 on 29 Apr 2026. They pledged about 850 KTPA and about Rs 5,000 cr. 'The next stage of the Scheme is project execution', and financial support depends on capacity development and start of production (S1, S2). As of this edition, neither PIB nor press coverage names the 58 entities, and we found no report of a disbursal. Among listed companies, only Eco Recycling has disclosed eligibility in an exchange filing (S5). Gravita's Q1 FY27 call and Q2 coverage do not mention the scheme (S7, S8).

Pledged investment (~Rs 5,000 cr) is about 0.6x the ~Rs 8,000 cr expected, while pledged capacity is about 3.1x the target (S1, S4). This suggests many pledges are low-capex pre-processing lines rather than refining.

blocks.title: BWMR minimum recovery target: EV and portable batteries
blocks.source: Source: IEA policy database, Lawrbit summary of BWMR 2022 (S21, S24)

items: Automotive and industrial batteries: 60% recovery by 2026-27 (S21).
EV batteries: minimum domestically recycled content starts at 5% in 2027-28 and rises to 20% by 2030-31. This creates captive demand for domestically refined salts (S21).
Producers that miss EPR targets pay environmental compensation (S21).

blocks.text: Materiality differs sharply. Gravita's Li-ion plant is about 1.2% of group capacity (6,000 of 4.97 lakh MTPA) (S6, S7). Its Q2 FY27 growth came from copper: consolidated revenue rose on the RMIL acquisition while standalone profit roughly halved on lead volume and scrap-sourcing disruptions (S9). Management attributes those disruptions partly to Gulf logistics, the source of 15-20% of its scrap (S7). Eco Recycling is much smaller. FY26 standalone revenue was Rs 48.18 cr (S5), so a capped Rs 25-50 cr incentive (S4) would be material. Neither company has disclosed Li-ion revenue or FY28 segment guidance, so we do not estimate an FY28 contribution.

Data cautions. (1) Gravita's Q2 consolidated revenue is reported as Rs 1,445.35 cr by one outlet (S8) and as Rs 1,427.35 cr net sales by another (S10), probably total income versus net sales. (2) A ScanX page reports Eco Recycling's FY26 revenue as 'Rs 481.8 crore' (S15). This looks like a 10x unit error against the filing-based Rs 4,818 lakh (S5).

blocks.text: Coverage by size: large caps (Hindalco, Tata Chemicals, Exide, Amara Raja) are mostly adjacency. Pure e-waste and Li-ion recyclers are all small caps: Eco Recycling at about Rs 789 cr and Namo eWaste at about Rs 778 cr market cap (S25). Mid caps are limited to Gravita and Pondy Oxides, and in both Li-ion is a small option. We found no mid-cap pure play. Lead-acid-only recyclers such as Jain Resource Recycling and NILE are excluded (S11).

blocks.title: Gravita and Eco Recycling: P/E, Jun 2026 vs Oct 2026

blocks.text: Multiples have compressed since June. Gravita's P/E has fallen from about 33x to 25.7x and its market cap from Rs 12,621 cr to Rs 10,244 cr. Eco Recycling's P/E has gone from about 37x to 32.9x and its market cap from Rs 853 cr to Rs 789 cr (S12, S25). The brief's 'Gravita ~+15% in 6 months' is contradicted by MarketsMojo's -19.28% one-year and -28.78% YTD returns as of 28 Oct (S10). On this evidence the market is paying for neither the scheme nor the refining option.

items: Ashika Institutional Equities (via Business Today, 26 Jul 2026) initiated on Gravita, Pondy Oxides and Jain Resource. It frames Indian metals as shifting from mining to recycling under BWMR and EPR formalisation. Its Gravita thesis rests on copper, lead capacity and value-added products, not Li-ion. It flags scrap availability, slow formalisation and scrap trade restrictions as risks (S11).
Gravita's Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT of about Rs 102 cr missed a market estimate of about Rs 107 cr (S9).

Analysts from Kotak Securities, Goldman Sachs, ICICI Securities and Mirae Asset Sharekhan were on Gravita's Q1 FY27 call. Only one Li-ion question was asked, about whether Gravita will go beyond black mass (S7).
Trade Brains, 'Top 3 e-waste management stocks' (23 Jun 2026): Gravita, Namo eWaste and Eco Recycling, citing their Li-ion facilities (S12).
EVreporter stakeholder survey (Nov 2025): Attero and Rubamin back black mass export curbs, Lohum and Namo eWaste prefer a phased approach, and Recykal calls for a transparent pricing index (S17).
We again found no Upstox article specific to this theme, so none is cited.
Feedstock scarcity: refiners are 'already short of feedstock' (S17), and Gravita says black mass quantity in India is low (S7).
Export arbitrage: overseas refiners pay higher payables, and some exporters misclassify black mass to avoid HS 8549 controls (S17).
Metal prices: black mass pricing is driven largely by cobalt content (S17).
Technology execution: no listed company runs a hydromet refinery. Gravita is at the R&D stage (S7), Eco Recycling does pre-processing only (S14), and Namo eWaste is seeking a partner (S22).
Disbursal timing: incentives are paid only after production starts, and opex support is back-ended (S1, S4).
Core-business drag: Gravita's standalone profit fell on lead scrap-sourcing disruption in Q2 FY27, so Li-ion optionality competes for attention and capital with copper and lead (S7, S9).

companies.name: Gravita India Ltd
companies.role: Diversified recycler (lead, aluminium, plastic, copper) with 4.97 lakh MTPA capacity. It commissioned a 6,000 MTPA Li-ion recycling pilot at Mundra in Jan 2026 for about Rs 14 cr and is doing R&D on a black mass processing unit (S6, S7).
companies.impact: Li-ion is about 1.2% of capacity and has no disclosed revenue. Q2 FY27 growth came from copper, while standalone profit fell (S8, S9). No public evidence of scheme eligibility. The theme is optionality within a Rs 1,680 cr capex plan, not an FY28 earnings driver (S7).

companies.name: Eco Recycling Ltd (Ecoreco)
companies.role: E-waste recycler and ITAD/EPR service provider with 25,200 MTPA e-waste and 6,000 MTPA Li-ion capacity at Vasai (S14).
companies.impact: The only listed name with a filed (provisional) scheme eligibility letter (S5). A capped incentive and the proposed Rs 100 cr recovery project (S15) would be large against Rs 16.20 cr quarterly standalone revenue (S16).

companies.name: Namo eWaste Management Ltd
companies.role: NSE SME-listed e-waste and battery recycler. Its 12,400 MTPA Li-ion recycling and refurbishing plant at Nashik produces black mass (S22).
companies.impact: A direct small-cap play on black mass. Domestic refining economics and export curbs matter most here, and its hydromet plan still lacks a technology partner (S17, S22).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
companies.role: Runs a PCB e-waste recycling plant at Pakhajan that recovers mainly copper plus rare earths and special metals (S18).
companies.impact: Urban mining feeds secondary copper to an integrated smelter. Small against group scale but aligned with critical-mineral policy (S18).

companies.name: Tata Chemicals Ltd
companies.role: Started commercial-pilot recovery of Li, Co, Ni and Mn from spent Li-ion cells near Mumbai, targeting 500 t (S19).
companies.impact: An early entrant with no recent scale-up disclosure found. Dormant optionality (S19).

companies.name: Pondy Oxides & Chemicals Ltd
companies.role: Lead and copper recycler. Took about a 0.29% stake in ACE Green Recycling to enter lead and lithium battery recycling (S20).
companies.impact: Li-ion is exploratory. Brokers value it on lead and copper expansion (S11).

companies.name: Exide Industries Ltd
companies.role: Li-ion cell, pack and module maker with Rs 4,902 cr invested. Its recycling arm is lead-only (S23).
companies.impact: A future source of gigafactory scrap and an EPR-obligated producer facing recycled-content mandates from 2027-28 (S21, S23).

companies.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a 60 MWh cell qualification plant in Jul 2026 under a 16 GWh gigafactory programme (S13).
companies.impact: Indirect exposure through gigafactory scrap and EPR obligations. No company-confirmed Li-ion recycling plant found (S13).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W42 edition, researched on 2026-11-01 with web search and direct page fetches. New this week: Gravita's Q2 FY27 results (27 Oct 2026, from Whalesbook, ScanX and MarketsMojo; the revenue figures differ between outlets and both are shown). Also new: Gravita's Q1 FY27 call transcript read directly, which updated group capacity to 4.97 lakh MTPA, the capex plan to Rs 1,680 cr and the Li-ion R&D commentary. Also added: Eco Recycling's Q1 FY27 standalone results and the PIB release on the 58 approvals, which replaces the NCMM portal as the primary source. The AIR scheme page was re-fetched. Market data is the screener.in snapshot in numbers.json (31 Oct 2026); Trade Brains (Jun 2026) is used for comparison. Dropped as stale or redundant: the Rubamin interview, the NCMM portal, the Hindustan Zinc tailings item and the Tradebrains battery-stocks list. No official list of the 58 entities, no subsidy disbursal and no Gravita scheme application was found. The brief's '+15% in 6 months' claim for Gravita is contradicted by dated return data and is shown as such. Some pages (PIB, ScanX) returned 403 on fetch and are cited from search-result content. Tata Chemicals' and Lawrbit's dates are approximate. No ratings or price targets are given.
